newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe's Sithole wants coup trial postponed.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe's Sithole wants coup trial postponed.

text.p: Veteran Zimbabwean opposition leader Ndabaningi Sithole applied on Monday for a postponement of his trial on charges of plotting to assassinate President Robert Mugabe, saying he was given little time to prepare his defence.

His lawyer, Tendai Biti, told a Harare high court that he had only received final prosecution documents from the state last Wednesday, and the first lot on October 23 when the trial date had been set for November 4.
"There was no adequate time to prepare the defence case, and further more the information supplied is scanty. The state approach is unfair and unreasonable," he told the packed court.

"And we are asking the court to postpone the trial because it would be unfair at this stage," Biti said, asking Justice James Devittie to order the state to provide adequate information to the defence.
State prosecution was due to make its submission to the court later on Monday before the judge rules on the application.
Sithole, 77, is facing three charges -- possession of arms, involvement in acts of sabotage and terrorism and conspiracy to murder President Mugabe, his political rival for over 30 years.
He was detained for two days a year ago over the allegations, but has been out on bail since.
Sithole denies the charges and accuses Mugabe of framing him to settle a personal vendetta.
